To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we performed a comprehensive analysis of DNA methylation in hemostatic genes and identified genetic variants that influence methylation and gene expression.
we have identified a number of novel SNPs that influence the methylation of hemostatic gene promoters in liver tissue, which in turn influences gene expression.

we identified 112 candidate allele-specific methylation single-nucleotide polymorphism (ASM-SNP) sites in hemostatic genes that are associated with the expression of their respective gene in human liver or other human tissues and with the levels of the respective plasma proteins, activities, or other relevant genome-wide association study (GWAS) traits.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of genetic and epigenetic variants that influence hemostatic factors in the human liver and the integration of this data with transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical data to identify novel mechanisms and biomarkers for hemostasis and thrombosis.
the genetic, epigenetics and transcriptome of human hemostatic genes.
the characterization of the genetic, epigenomic, and transcriptomic landscape of hemostatic factors in human liver tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our study provides the first high-resolution map of the DNA-methylation landscape of hemostatic gene in human liver tissue and suggests that methlation regulated by genetic variants may provide a mechanistical link between non-coding SNPs and variation in circulating hemostatis proteins, prothrobic disease and drug responses.

our data provide evidence that ASM-SNPs in cis may play a role in regulating gene expression, which in turn affects the levels of plasma proteins, and that some of these variants are associated with prothrombotics diseases and drug response.

we have provided the first detailed map and analysis of the DNA methylome of hemostatic gene in human liver tissue and that this may provide a mechanistically relevant link between genetic variants and variation in circulating hemostasis proteins, thrombotic diseases, as well as drug response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genetic variants can influence DNA methylaion in cis which can in turn affect gene expression and ultimately circulating levels of hemostatic proteins.
we have identified 112 SNPs that are associated with DNA methylation in the liver.

we performed the first comprehensive DNA methylation and ASM analysis in human liver tissue and identified a number of SNPs that may be involved in the regulation of hemostatic gene expression and plasma protein levels through DNA methylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic variation of hemostatic traits can be influenced by DNA methylation in a gene specific manner and this is a mechanism that needs to be taken into account for future studies.
we have identified a set of genetic variants that influence the expression of hemostatic factors by altering their methylation status in the liver.

the DNA methylation status of hemostatic loci can be affected by cis genetic variation, which in turn can influence expression levels of hemostatic proteins and their association with disease and drug response.
